correctness.rationale: Every proper convex quadrilateral admits affine chart A=(t,0), B=(0,s), C=(t-1,0), D=(0,s-1) for 0<t,s<1; shoelace area is 1/2. All six unordered vertex differences give precisely the diagonal square constraints |x|<=1,|y|<=1 and the four listed side constraints. In opposite-sign quadrants the two minus-type constraints have coefficient sums t+s and 2-t-s: at most one removes the corner pair, with two equal triangle areas and total delta_minus^2/M_minus. In same-sign quadrants the plus constraints have sums 1+t-s and 1+s-t and remove the complementary corner pair, total delta_plus^2/M_plus; cuts cannot overlap in positive area. Intersecting with the square, polar area is 4-delta_minus^2/M_minus-delta_plus^2/M_plus, times 1/2 yields the exact formula. Interior transition lines have zero cut. Both deficits vanish iff t+s=1 and t=s, i.e. t=s=1/2, equivalent to a parallelogram. Eggleston Theorem 1.1 gives strict mu>3/2 for every genuine four-vertex polygon since equality is triangular. Along t=s=r, r in [1/2,1), mu=2-(2r-1)^2/(2r^2) decreases continuously from 2 to 3/2, giving full image (3/2,2]. Independent exact-rational clipping of all ordered difference half-planes confirms 368 distinct prescribed/random rational pairs and four diagonal-path checks; finite checks are not the proof.
residual_risks: No general higher-polygon or higher-dimensional conclusion; t and s endpoints correspond to degenerations.
Finite rational checks verify only tested points, not arbitrary real parameters.

value.rationale: The planar quadrilateral is the first non-triangular polytope and its two affine diagonal ratios give a natural complete moduli chart. The Makai/Eggleston polar-difference volume product is a standard affine-invariant quantity used in sharp inequalities and stability theory. Computing its complete nonconstant profile, its full attainable interval, and its unique maximizing affine class is an exact reusable benchmark for restricted-body extremal and stability analysis. It is not simply a parameter rename or a known universal-bound recomputation: the shape-dependent rational terms are not implied by the known inequalities. It is an elementary two-dimensional calculation, not a universal sharp inequality, and its value should not be exaggerated.
residual_risks: The computation is elementary given the polar inequalities; object/invariant completeness, not technical complexity, supplies the significance.
No universal quantitative stability modulus or polygon-count extension is claimed.

limitations: Genuine convex quadrilaterals only: 0<t,s<1. The lower endpoint 3/2 is not attained by a proper quadrilateral.
Affine product uses the unscaled polar difference body; scaling (Q-Q)/2 multiplies by four.
